title: When One App Rules Them All: The Case of WeChat and Mobile in China

reader_summary.headline: When One App Rules Them All, the Case of WeChat and Mobile in China by Connie Chan.
reader_summary.overview: When One App Rules Them All, the Case of WeChat and Mobile in China by Connie Chan, first published August 2015. You can also find and share this essay at A6C.com slash mobile first China. This post is all about WeChat, but it's also about more than just WeChat.

key_points.text: While seemingly just a messaging app, WeChat is actually more of a portal, a platform, and even a mobile operating system.
key_points.evidence_quote: While seemingly just a messaging app, WeChat is actually more of a portal, a platform, and even a mobile operating system, depending how you look at it.

key_points.text: Much has been written about WeChat on the context of messaging app.
key_points.evidence_quote: Much has been written about WeChat on the context of messaging app.

key_points.text: but few outside of China really understand how it works.
key_points.evidence_quote: but few outside of China really understand how it works, and how it can pull off what for many companies and countries is still a far-off vision of a world managed entirely through our smartphones.

key_points.text: Many of WeChat's most interesting features, such as access to city services, are not even visible to users outside of China.
key_points.evidence_quote: Many of WeChat's most interesting features, such as access to city services, are not even visible to users outside of China.
